answer: Every agent identity must post a bond that is slashed on proven duplication, so registering n fake agents costs n times that stake rather than n free calls. Regulators anchor each name to one attested key, and any grove of proof linking two names burns the shared deposit at once. Auditors earn only for unique findings, so copying another's wharf of work pays nothing while the slashed stake funds future bounties. Marginal attack cost therefore grows linearly with fleet size while honest yield per agent stays flat, making a mass syndicate an ocean of collateral waiting to dissolve.
